subject: biology
title: Viral life cycles: lytic and lysogenic
key_idea: A virus cannot reproduce outside a host cell. In the lytic pathway it takes over the cell, makes new viruses and bursts the cell open. In the lysogenic pathway its genetic material is inserted into the host's genome and the virus stays hidden for a time.

blocks.text: In the lytic pathway a virus reproduces straight away and destroys the host cell. This section covers the stages in order.

items.meaning: The living cell a virus infects. Viruses cannot replicate outside a host.
The host cell bursts open, releasing the new virus particles.
The virus uses the host cell to make new viruses, then lyses the cell.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of the lytic pathway in order, from the virus binding to the host cell to the cell lysing.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of the lytic pathway in order.
steps: The virus binds to the host cell
The virus inserts its genetic material into the host cell
The host cell machinery makes viral proteins and genetic material
New virus particles assemble inside the cell
The host cell lyses and the new viruses are released

items: Many virus particles are produced from one infected cell.
The viruses leave the host and are released into body fluids.
They can spread through airborne droplets or by contact to another host.
The cycle then repeats in the new host's cells.
The virus uses the host cell machinery to make its own parts.
New viruses assemble inside the cell, which then lyses to release them.
Many viruses are released, so infection spreads to other cells and other hosts.

blocks.text: In the lysogenic pathway the virus does not destroy the cell at once. Its genetic material is inserted into the genome of the host.

items: The viral genetic material becomes part of the host's genome.
The host cell survives and is not lysed at this stage.
The viral genetic material is copied each time the host cell divides.
Later the virus can enter the lytic pathway and produce new viruses.

rows: Used straight away to make new viruses
Inserted into the genome of the host

items: A **bacteriophage** is a virus that infects bacterial cells.
Used through the lytic pathway, it kills bacteria, so it could be an alternative to antibiotics.
This could reduce the problem of antibiotic resistance.
Bacteriophages do not affect animal cells, and they replicate themselves.
Lysogenic: viral genetic material is inserted into the host genome.
Lytic: viruses are made at once and the host cell lyses.
Bacteriophages infect bacterial cells and can kill them by lysis.

checks.q: Describe the lytic pathway for a virus.
checks.a: The virus uses the host cell machinery. Viral genetic material and proteins are made. New virus particles assemble. The host cell lyses to release the viruses.

checks.q: The genetic material of a virus can be inserted into the genome of the host. Name this type of pathway.
Explain how the lytic pathway spreads infection through a population.
checks.a: Many virus particles are produced from one infected cell. They leave the host and are released into body fluids. They spread through airborne droplets or contact to another host.

exam_phrases: virus inserts its genetic material into the host cell
uses the host cell machinery / organelles / resources
virus components are assembled inside the cell
cell lyses to release the virus
bacteriophage do not affect animal cells

mistakes.wrong: The virus enters a cell and reproduces, divides and grows.
mistakes.right: "The virus enters a cell" and "reproduces / divides / grows" are ignored. Say it uses the host cell machinery to make viral components, which assemble inside the cell.

mistakes.wrong: The host lyses and the viruses are released.
mistakes.right: "The host lyses" is ignored. Say the cell lyses (or the host cell bursts) to release the viruses.

mistakes.wrong: In the lytic pathway the viral genetic material joins the host genome and waits.
mistakes.right: That is lysogenic. A lytic answer uses the host cell machinery at once, assembles new viruses and lyses the cell, with no lysogenic steps.

worked_example.question: Viruses can cause disease. Describe how the lytic pathway is involved in the reproduction of viruses.
answer_points: Virus inserts its genetic material into the host cell.
Uses the host cell machinery, organelles or resources, and virus components (protein, genetic material) are made.
Virus components are assembled inside the cell.
Cell lyses to release the virus, or viruses are released from the cell.
worked_example.tip: Follow the stages in order. Accept: it takes over the host cell, or the host cell bursts.
